name: Heat contracting (Wärmelieferung) in rented buildings
summary: A landlord outsources heat generation and supply to a contractor who installs, runs and maintains the heating plant; the cost is passed on to tenants through heating bills.
how_it_makes_money: The contractor sells heat at a price formula agreed with the landlord. Capital costs and profit are included in the price that tenants end up paying.

hardware: Heating plant, often continuing to run the existing gas boiler

stakeholder_value.customer: Landlord: no investment and less risk; tenants: not clearly better off

what_must_be_true: Cost neutrality for tenants can be shown or avoided
Landlord-contractor relationships stay acceptable to regulators and tenants

risks_failure_causes.text: Journalists and tenant groups report that price formulas are factually wrong, ineffective or contested and tenant costs rise
The German Tenants' Association demands binding rules and a price cap for heat supply contracts in rented buildings
Contractors that are subsidiaries of the landlord weaken the efficiency incentive; often the old gas boiler simply keeps running

cases.note: Around four million apartments are supplied under contracting contracts according to industry figures, but how many benefit financially is questioned. Consumer groups estimate at least hundreds of thousands of tenants pay too much.

sources.title: Utopia: Hunderttausende Mieter zahlen zu hohe Heizkosten (Correctiv research)
